take: Brent’s $8.94 (8.6%) collapse to $94.66 on Wednesday, as the White House tied the midterm rout to the Iran war and traders priced an end to the conflict, is the dominant crude signal and should steepen the back end of the curve whilst pressuring product cracks that have been carried by war-risk premium. The same de-escalation narrative cuts against the freight complex: any Hormuz reopening would compress tonne-miles and war-risk insurance, even as the UAE weighs a third bypass pipeline and Qatar becomes the largest buyer of US LNG, both of which entrench longer-haul gas flows. The inventory angle is the refinery run-rate: US utilisation averaged above 95% between May and September, the highest since 1998, yet global refinery inputs fell 4.8 million b/d (6%) in 2Q26 after the conflict began, so any peace dividend arrives into a system already running hot and vulnerable to a product stock build. Watch the butane complex as the cross-market tell — NWE November butane at $1,125/t, a 30-year high, is pricing LPG tightness that will not unwind on a crude selloff alone and will keep petchem and blending economics stretched against falling crude. The next 24 hours hinge on whether the selloff extends or stabilises: watch for official comment on Iran talks, any Hormuz transit update, and whether the polar vortex signal into Northwest Europe firms gas and, by substitution, gasoil and bunker spreads.

items.title: Global refinery inputs fell sharply in the second quarter of 2026 before modest recovery
items.summary: Global crude oil refinery inputs fell by 4.8 million barrels per day (b/d) in the second quarter of 2026 (2Q26), or 6%, following the start of conflict in late February in the Middle East, according to data from Kpler. Throughput then increased by 1.8 million b/d in the third quarter, primarily as refiners in the region adjusted to new trade flows.

items.title: LNG imports make up increasing share of Colombia's natural gas supply
items.summary: Colombia is importing more liquefied natural gas (LNG) as domestic production continues to fall. A potential drought this fall and winter could limit the availability of hydroelectric generation and boost the country's demand for natural gas power generation. Colombia's government has declared a national disaster in anticipation of a drought resulting from an expected strong El Niño.

items.title: U.S. refineries have been running at very high rates in 2026
items.summary: The U.S. refinery fleet has run at higher-than-normal rates this year, with refinery utilization averaging more than 95% of capacity between May and September, the highest for those months since 1998. Tight global product supplies this year have boosted margins for petroleum products, particularly for diesel, incentivizing the increased run rates.
